name: Ethnan
overview: Ethnan was a male member of the tribe of Judah, uniquely identified as the son of Ashhur and Helah. His mention is brief and specific, without additional narrative or descriptive notes. He is recorded in Scripture simply as a descendant within the Judahite lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Ethnan is a proper name found in 1 Chronicles 4:7 and is noted to mean "hire [of a prostitute?]". This meaning is given without indication that the name was divinely given, and it stands as a distinct Hebrew personal name within the genealogical record.
familyAndRelationships: Ethnan's family relationships are explicitly recorded as the son of Ashhur and Helah, confirming his place in the Judahite genealogy. Scripture does not provide further familial details beyond these parents.
scriptureSignificance: Ethnan's significance lies in his inclusion within the genealogical records of the tribe of Judah, emphasizing the biblical theme of lineage and God's providential preservation of His people. Although no additional narrative is attached to him, his presence in 1 Chronicles 4:7 contributes to the comprehensive genealogical framework that undergirds the historical and spiritual heritage of Israel.
